sketchMechanisms: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily upon first access.
A type declared with no constructors (`Void`) can never be instantiated — values of that type cannot exist at the term level, yet the type itself can be named and passed around.
The `weak` reference modifier means the runtime may deallocate the referent at any time, and accessing it yields an Optional — presence that may already be nil.
